item.content:encoded:
A Year 8 student of Korovuto Primary School is calling for stronger action against drug dealers targeting young people, while stressing that education, rehabilitation and family support are equally important in protecting children from drugs.

Speaking during a consultation on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026, Krystal K umar questioned whether the Government is doing enough to prevent illegal drugs from reaching schools and communities.

Kumar also raised concerns about whether children are being properly educated about the dangers of drugs before they face pressure to try them.

She says fighting drugs requires more than punishment, stressing the need for early prevention, counselling, rehabilitation and effective law enforcement.

The 14-year-old believes young people who make mistakes should not automatically be treated as having no future, but should instead receive guidance and support to make better choices.

The student also called for schools to provide safe learning environments, while families and communities should support young people through sports, education, cultural activities and youth programmes.

Kumar has urged the Joint Committee to carefully consider how the proposed constitutional changes could affect the rights, safety and future of children.

She says any changes to the Constitution should be clearly explained to the public, with young people also given an opportunity to share their views.

The student stressed that although they are only in Year 8, age should not prevent young people from speaking up on issues affecting their future.

Kumar also says protecting children from drugs is a shared responsibility involving the Government, schools, families and communities.

item.title: Namara representative calls for GCC recognition, provincial Senate representation and removal of FICAC
item.description: The Mata-ni-Tikina of Namara, Sekaia Mua, is calling for the Great Council of Chiefs to be formally recognised under the proposed constitutional changes, provincial representation in the Senate and the removal of the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption. Mua raised these issues while making his submission to the Joint Parliamentary Select Committee on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 20
item.content:encoded:
The Mata-ni-Tikina of Namara, Sekaia Mua, is calling for the Great Council of Chiefs to be formally recognised under the proposed constitutional changes, provincial representation in the Senate and the removal of the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption.

Mua raised these issues while making his submission to the Joint Parliamentary Select Committee on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 at Vunimono Hall in Nausori.

He says the Great Council of Chiefs plays an important role in protecting iTaukei culture, traditions and the interests of indigenous communities.

Mua believes the removal of the Council in the past weakened the traditional authority and identity of indigenous Fijians, and says its role should be strengthened under the proposed constitutional changes.

He also supports provincial representation in the Senate, saying this would help maintain the traditional chiefly system and ensure provincial voices are represented.

On FICAC, Mua called for the Commission to be removed, arguing that corruption investigations should instead be handled by the Fiji Police Force.

He questioned FICAC's effectiveness and raised concerns about how corruption cases are handled.

Mua also urged the Committee not to rush the proposed referendum, saying people in villages and rural communities must be given enough time to understand the proposed constitutional changes before making a decision.

He says the Government must ensure the concerns of indigenous Fijians are heard and their interests protected when decisions are made about the country's future.

Meanwhile, Mua also highlighted the serious water shortage affecting people in Namara, Tailevu, saying some families have been forced to use a water source previously declared unsafe by the Ministry of Health.

He says villagers have no alternative water supply, while dry conditions continue to affect their access to clean drinking water.

Mua says the Water Authority of Fiji delivered water on one occasion, but no further supplies have been received.

He says residents have been requesting a proper water supply for years and are still waiting for a lasting solution.

Mua, who has served as Mata-ni-Tikina for four years, says villagers continue to ask him when assistance will arrive.

He is calling on the Government and the Water Authority of Fiji to urgently address the shortage, saying rural communities should not be forgotten.

item.title: Buretu Village woman calls for equality and peace, questions Christian State proposal
item.description: We cannot say that we keep on enforcing our Christian state, but some of our iTaukei Christian boys are burning Hindu temples and calling them names. That is not equality. That is the concern raised by Amalagi Kolikata of Buretu Village while making a submission to the Joint Committee on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 at Vunimono Hall in Nausori.
item.content:encoded:
We cannot say that we keep on enforcing our Christian state, but some of our iTaukei Christian boys are burning Hindu temples and calling them names. That is not equality.

That is the concern raised by Amalagi Kolikata of Buretu Village while making a submission to the Joint Committee on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 at Vunimono Hall in Nausori.

Kolikata is urging political leaders to promote peace and prioritise the basic needs of the people ahead of the next general election.

She says people want progress and growth for their children and families, regardless of whether they live in rural or urban communities.

Kolikata believes the current political focus will not help the people at this point, saying leaders should instead address issues affecting their daily lives.

She says the priorities should include crime prevention, healthcare and education, including ensuring children return to school and have access to tertiary education.

Kolikata Â also believes addressing these issues would encourage more people to participate and show their support.

She also raised concerns about crime-related content shared on social media, saying children could be exposed to such content through their parents accounts and develop similar views.

Kolikata called on political leaders to promote peace and work towards a Fiji envisioned by its ancestors, where no one is left out.

The consultation continues in Nadi and Lautoka today.

item.title: Proposed One United Republican Party applies for registration
item.description: Registrar of Political Parties Ana Mataiciwa says the FEO is preparing to publish the application in a newspaper and the Government Gazette, as required under the Political Parties (Registration, Conduct, Funding and Disclosures) Act 2013. She says members of the public will be able to submit written objections to the proposed party's registration during the objection period following publication.
item.content:encoded:
Registrar of Political Parties Ana Mataiciwa says the FEO is preparing to publish the application in a newspaper and the Government Gazette, as required under the Political Parties (Registration, Conduct, Funding and Disclosures) Act 2013.

She says members of the public will be able to submit written objections to the proposed party's registration during the objection period following publication.

Mataiciwa says all objections received will be forwarded to the proposed party within seven days for a response.

She says the FEO will then assess the objections and responses before informing both the objectors and the proposed party of its decision.

The proposed OUR Party will be informed whether its application has been approved or rejected after a thorough assessment of its compliance with the legal requirements.

The FEO says transparency and public participation are important in ensuring that political parties meet the necessary legal requirements.

item.title: Taveuni families could save on medical travel costs as hospital upgrades improve patient care
item.description: Families in Taveuni could save on travel costs for specialist medical treatment in the future, as upgrades to Taveuni Hospital improve patient care and create opportunities for more services to be provided closer to home. Senior Divisional Medical Officer at Taveuni Hospital, Dr Sapeta Taito, says the improvements are providing patients with a cleaner, safer and more comfortable environment while
item.content:encoded:
Families in Taveuni could save on travel costs for specialist medical treatment in the future, as upgrades to Taveuni Hospital improve patient care and create opportunities for more services to be provided closer to home.

Senior Divisional Medical Officer at Taveuni Hospital, Dr Sapeta Taito, says the improvements are providing patients with a cleaner, safer and more comfortable environment while receiving treatment and recovering from illness.

Dr Taito says the renovated wards now have better lighting, working fans and cleaner washrooms, making a difference to patients staying at the hospital.

She says while these may seem like small improvements, they are important for patients' comfort and recovery.

Dr Taito says the upgrades have also improved working conditions for doctors and nurses, allowing them to focus more on patient care with fewer disruptions caused by ageing facilities.

She says some Taveuni residents currently have to travel to other areas for specialist medical services, placing an additional financial burden on families.

However, she hopes the improved facilities will attract more visiting specialist medical teams, allowing patients to receive treatment closer to home and could reducing travel expenses.

The redevelopment includes a new cyclone-resistant roof, improvements to the operating theatre, maternity and emergency departments, and upgrades to water, electricity and safety systems.

The work is being carried out in stages to ensure patients continue to receive essential medical services while improvements are underway.

The hospital upgrade is being supported by the Australian Government in partnership with Fiji's Ministry of Health and Medical Services through the Fiji-Australia Vuvale Partnership.

item.title: Over 1,000 patients receive skin treatment during five-day outreach in Kadavu
item.description: The Ministry of Health and Medical Services says 70 to 80 percent of the patients treated were children. The government-funded outreach was conducted by the Dermatology Department at PJ Twomey Hospital, covering communities from Daviqele to Naqara.
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Health and Medical Services says 70 to 80 percent of the patients treated were children.

The government-funded outreach was conducted by the Dermatology Department at PJ Twomey Hospital, covering communities from Daviqele to Naqara.

The Ministry says medical teams treated more than 200 patients in each zone.

Health Ministry says scabies and fungal infections, including tinea capitis, identified was the most common skin conditions.

Patients were provided with medication and advice on preventing the spread of these infections.

Vunisea Subdivisional Hospital Medical Officer Dr Aaron Prasad says he has never seen such a large turnout for a medical outreach programme.

He says he was particularly impressed by the interest shown by patients and parents in understanding their conditions and learning how to prevent infections.

Dr Prasad says the response demonstrates the willingness of people in Kadavu to seek medical treatment and take care of their health.

item.title: Tropical Cyclone Wati forms near Cook Islands, no direct threat to Fiji
item.description: They say th e cyclone is currently moving southeast towards the Cook Islands, with forecasts indicating that it could intensify further. While Fiji is not in the direct path of the cyclone, the Weather Office says it will continue to monitor the system and provide updates.
item.content:encoded:
They say th e cyclone is currently moving southeast towards the Cook Islands, with forecasts indicating that it could intensify further.

While Fiji is not in the direct path of the cyclone, the Weather Office says it will continue to monitor the system and provide updates.

Communities in the Cook Islands, particularly those along the cyclone's forecast path, to remain alert and follow advisories from their local weather and emergency authorities.
